A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ECG-R1 and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-F. Matching relocated and renumbered material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original ECG interpretation experiments, modality robustness evaluations, cardiologist ratings, and appendix ablations and benchmark results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds GLM-5 evaluation scores and cardiologist ratings for additional models.

M1.justification: The protocol-guided corpus construction, decoupled encoders, Interleaved Modality Dropout, SFT, and EDER reinforcement learning remain unchanged. The numerical supervision and uncertainty estimation mentioned in C.7 are future proposals, not implemented components.

E1.justification: Training data, the ECG-Grounding test set, five ECG-Bench datasets, and missing-modality and cardiologist evaluation tasks are retained. GLM-5 evaluates existing outputs; no additional dataset, population, or input scenario is documented.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds GPT-5.1-Instant and PULSE to the cardiologist comparison previously containing GEM and ECG-R1. The automatic benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. GLM-5 serves as an evaluator rather than a competing ECG model.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 and new Appendix C.2 add independent grading by GLM-5 under the existing rubric, alongside DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus. Original splits, metrics, training settings, and the stated four-cardiologist, 100-case design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2 tests whether the interpretation findings persist with a different evaluator, providing a sensitivity check for evaluator-specific judgments. Existing corpus comparisons, IMD and EDER ablations, evaluator case examples, and Appendix E case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 extends the existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting to additional models without changing statistical procedures. Seed information is unchanged, and no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added. Calibrated uncertainty estimation appears only as future work.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, with supplementary GLM-5 scores and two cardiologist-rating rows added. New Table 4 reports diagnosis scores of 83.29 for ECG-R1 RL and 78.99 for GEM, but GEM leads on Lead Evidence Validity, 4.87 versus 4.66. These reflect a different judge, not a same-setting performance gain. C.7 also asserts benefits outside frequent report patterns without subgroup scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, coverage assumption, robustness and consistency theorems in Section 2.4, and complete proofs in Appendix D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning protocol guidance, modality robustness, evidence rewards, and unreliable existing ECG interpretations. Adding 'ECG' to 'reasoning MLLM' does not materially change the already ECG-specific novelty claim.

C2.justification: New C.7 identifies limitations from frequent-report-focused RL and uneven QT/QTc numerical supervision. C.2 discusses evaluator-specific bias, and Section 3.5 interprets PULSE's accuracy versus completeness tradeoff. The Impact Statement adds more specific deployment qualifications, including multi-site validation and monitoring.

D1.justification: V1's abstract explicitly advertises code, data, and an online platform; v2 retains the same code repository link but removes the data-availability statement and platform link. This reduces documented access information without establishing that resources were withdrawn. Hardware, hyperparameters, and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wang et al. references on physiological waveform reasoning and SE-diff, removes the Liu et al. ECG review and Google/OpenAI announcement references, and retains the substantive Appendix A positioning. M3-embedding and Chiron-o1 bibliographic updates concern existing works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and terminology edits, updates affiliations and publication information, adds conflict disclosures and acknowledgements, and inserts evaluator and limitations subsections in Appendix C. The overall narrative and organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the GLM-5 results table and expands Table 3 with two rows. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and repositioned, with accompanying text reflow. Figures 1-11 retain identical image content; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The GLM-5 cross-check reduces dependence on DeepSeek for automatic evaluation, which also generated training supervision. Broader cardiologist comparisons and specific limitations modestly strengthen evidence and transparency. These benefits are partly offset by reduced data/platform access information and incomplete integration of the new human comparisons: Section 3.2 still describes ratings only for GEM and ECG-R1.
